title: Guitar lessons through Edgar B. Stern and symphony players
summary: A patron who bought instruments for the symphony had symphony musicians teach him piano methods and reading.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What does he do? What did he get money for?

Well, different funds. He come in there to buy instruments for the symphony, you know, when he's about to go out of business. What's his name? He gave Shirley a lift too. I can't call his name. I don't know. It could be Stern. Yeah, Edgar B. Stern. Edgar B. Stern came in there to buy instruments in Groomwolf, and he heard me play, and he was teasing me one day, he'd say, well I'll teach you how to play the guitar. If you buy me a drink, I'd say okay. I did. So, 3521 Diffin Street, well they started to send in different men out of the symphony, on my oil fee, because I collected insurance since 1939 at that time. And they used to send those different artists down there, and they put them in the standard piano methods, and I just about went through the whole ten of them, you know. How to Melody, and How to Read Bad, both treble clef and bass clef. And from then on I bought different books and advanced myself.
